attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The paraphrase is close to the words. But 'most expensive scientific experiments in history' and 'down the drain' are hyperbole and a value judgment. They work as rhetoric, not as a checkable observation, so 'observation' is the wrong kind.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no cost basis, no list to compare against, and no test for waste. Any verdict would rest on choices the evaluator made, not the speaker. Treating the claim as not_applicable is fair.

evidence.note: Meta's own disclosure of 2025 capex across the whole company. Not the cost of a single 'experiment', and silent on waste.
Confirms Musk's 'not built right' admission and the founder departures. Gives no cost figure and no finding that money was lost.
Backs the premise that Meta's model fell short, but measures neither cost nor waste.
Published before the evaluation date. Reports Muse Spark as competitive, which cuts against waste, but the claim has no measure to test this against.

reviews.rationale: This is a rhetorical, evaluative statement. It sets no cost basis and no list of experiments to rank against, and gives no test for 'down the drain'. The evidence confirms the premises (Meta's model fell short, xAI is being rebuilt) and shows partial counterevidence (Muse Spark was competitive). But no evidence can settle a value judgment that has no measure.
